Focus areas

What we research

REPro works in one place, across four connected topics.

Maternal health

Pregnancy, birth, and the postpartum year — including the policy that shapes outcomes in it.

Reproductive health

Access, autonomy, and the systems that determine who gets care, and when.

Child & family health

Outcomes that extend past the parent to the family unit they return home to.

Health equity

Who bears risk unequally in this data, and what a policy or program could close.

Services

Two ways to work together

One gets a client-ready dashboard in front of your team quickly. The other goes deeper, when a program or policy decision needs a fuller evidence base.

Lead engagement

Data-to-Decision

We take your claims, encounter, or program data and turn it into a client-ready dashboard and decision brief — built to sit in front of a board, a state legislature, or a funder, not a shared drive.

  • Data cleaning & integration — from raw exports to an analysis-ready dataset.
  • Descriptive & policy-comparative analysis — your population benchmarked against state and national context.
  • A dashboard built around your decision — not a general-purpose report.
  • A short brief translating findings into recommended next steps.
Mixed-methods

Research & Evaluation

Deeper qualitative and evaluative work for organizations building or assessing a maternal health program — from a new virtual care model to a state policy pilot.

  • Qualitative interviewing & synthesis — patient, provider, and stakeholder voice alongside the numbers.
  • Program & implementation evaluation — including RCT and quasi-experimental designs.
  • Literature synthesis & evidence briefs — grounded in the current policy literature.
  • Turning CDC Maternal Mortality Review Committee findings into an implementation plan.

Most Data-to-Decision engagements are scoped and priced per project — typically 4–8 weeks, not billed hourly. Research & Evaluation engagements are scoped individually based on methods and timeline.

How it works

From first email to finished brief

1

Discovery call

We talk through the decision you're trying to make and what data you already have.

2

Scope & quote

You get a written scope, timeline, and price before anything starts.

3

Analysis & build

Data cleaning, analysis, and dashboard or brief development, with check-ins along the way.

4

Delivery & walkthrough

You get the finished deliverable, plus a working session to walk through findings and next steps.

Data & confidentiality

Built to handle sensitive health data responsibly

BAA on request

REPro can execute a Business Associate Agreement for any engagement that involves protected health information.

Minimum-necessary use

Data is used only for the scoped analysis it was provided for — never repurposed, sold, or shared beyond the engagement.

Secure handling, start to finish

Files are transferred and stored securely, and returned or deleted once the engagement closes.

Approach

Principles we work by

Public-sector fluency

Comfortable in Medicaid claims data, state legislative language, and the CDC and KFF literature that shapes this field — so findings arrive in terms your stakeholders already use.

Built for one decision

Every deliverable is scoped to the choice it needs to inform, not a general-purpose report that gets filed away unread.

Mixed-methods by default

Qualitative and quantitative evidence are combined from the start, not run in parallel and left for your team to reconcile.

About

"Reproductive health disparities persist because too many policies are built without the evidence to close them. I founded REPro to change that — pairing rigorous data analysis with a relentless focus on the outcomes that matter for women and families."

— Molly Waymouth

Molly Waymouth is a health policy researcher and analyst whose work focuses on evaluating innovative, technology-enabled care models and policy structures to advance health equity and dismantle barriers to care for underserved populations. Her research centers on maternal, perinatal, and women's health, with extensive expertise spanning randomized clinical trial design, implementation science, and macro-level societal impact modeling.

Her scholarship bridges mixed-methods clinical evaluation — such as assessing the equity, acceptability, and clinical outcomes of telelactation, virtual doula care, and remote monitoring programs — with high-level policy research examining the return on investment for women's health research funding and systemic access barriers across healthcare systems.

Credentials
  • Former Senior Policy Analyst — RAND (12 years)
  • Former Health Insurance Specialist — CMS/HHS Philadelphia Regional Office
  • DrPH Candidate, Women's Reproductive Health — Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
  • MPH, Health Management & Policy — Drexel University
